_comment: The 28 investigation criteria. Each lists catalog variable ids in priority order. status: live = official monthly series with a long record; proxy = no direct series, the variables measure something related (say so); short_record = data exist but are too short for trend testing yet; not_trendable = no public monthly series (imagery only). Variable ids missing from the catalog are dropped at load time and reported.

criteria.name: Temperature
criteria.definition: How warm the air near the ground is.

criteria.name: Rainfall / Precipitation
criteria.definition: Water falling from the sky as rain or snow, usually in millimetres per day or month.

criteria.name: Sea Surface Temperature
criteria.definition: How warm the top layer of the ocean is.

criteria.name: Evaporation
criteria.definition: Water moving from soil, lakes and plants into the air (evapotranspiration).

criteria.name: Streamflow
criteria.definition: How much water flows down a river, in cubic metres per second.
criteria.note: Measured streamflow (USGS gauges) and NLDAS model streamflow cover the United States only; elsewhere GLDAS runoff and baseflow are the closest global proxies.

criteria.name: Ozone
criteria.definition: The total amount of ozone gas above a place, in Dobson Units; most of it is in the stratosphere.

criteria.name: Chlorophyll
criteria.definition: The green pigment of microscopic ocean plants (phytoplankton); more chlorophyll means more plankton.

criteria.name: Surface Wind
criteria.definition: How fast the wind blows near the surface.

criteria.name: Sea Ice
criteria.definition: Frozen ocean water floating at the poles; extent is the ocean area with at least 15% ice cover.
criteria.note: Sea-ice extent is a whole-hemisphere number, not a value for the drawn box.

criteria.name: Oil Pollution
criteria.definition: Oil spilled or leaked on the sea surface, seen by radar satellites as dark, smooth patches.
criteria.note: No public monthly oil-slick series exists. Slicks are found one image at a time in radar imagery.

criteria.name: Water Surface Elevation
criteria.definition: The height of the water surface of a river, lake or reservoir above a reference level.
criteria.note: SWOT measures water heights worldwide but only since 2023, too short for a trend test; USGS gauges give long US records.

criteria.name: Lake Water Level
criteria.definition: How high the water stands in a lake.

criteria.name: River Water Level
criteria.definition: How high the water stands in a river at a gauge (gage height).

criteria.name: Reservoir Water Level
criteria.definition: How high the water stands behind a dam.

criteria.name: Ocean Surface Elevation
criteria.definition: The height of the sea surface; its long-term rise is sea-level rise.

criteria.name: Atmospheric composition
criteria.definition: The gases and particles in the air: pollution such as nitrogen dioxide, smoke and dust, and carbon dioxide.

criteria.name: Atmospheric temperature
criteria.definition: Temperature of the air above the ground, up to the tropopause (about 10–16 km high).

criteria.name: Land surface conditions
criteria.definition: The state of the ground surface: how hot it is and how wet the topsoil is.

criteria.name: Vegetation / Ecosystem condition
criteria.definition: How green and productive the plants are.

criteria.name: Wetland extent
criteria.definition: The area covered by marshes, swamps and other wetlands.
criteria.note: No monthly wetland-area series exists. These variables track how wet the land is, which is related but is not wetland area.

where_to_look.name: MODIS land cover MCD12Q1, 'permanent wetlands' class (yearly, via AppEEARS)

criteria.name: Forest condition
criteria.definition: How healthy and productive a forest is, seen through greenness and photosynthesis.
criteria.note: Measures forest condition, not forest area. Draw the box over forest.

criteria.name: Coastal change
criteria.definition: How coastlines move and change: erosion, flooding and sea-level rise.
criteria.note: No public monthly shoreline-position series exists. Relative sea level at the coast is the closest measured driver.

criteria.name: Agricultural conditions
criteria.definition: Growing conditions for crops: greenness, soil water, rainfall and water use.

criteria.name: Surface water extent
criteria.definition: The area covered by lakes, rivers and flooded land.
criteria.note: No long monthly water-area series exists. Water storage and water levels are related but are not area.

where_to_look.name: OPERA Dynamic Surface Water Extent (2023 onward, too short for trends)

criteria.name: Soil moisture
criteria.definition: How much water is in the top layer of the soil.

criteria.name: Snow / Ice conditions
criteria.definition: How much snow is on the ground (as water) and how much sea ice there is.

criteria.name: Surface roughness / Radar backscatter
criteria.definition: How strongly a surface reflects radar pulses back to the satellite; rough or wet surfaces look brighter.
criteria.note: Radar backscatter comes as images that must be calibrated and processed scene by scene; no public monthly series exists.

criteria.name: Ship / Maritime activity
criteria.definition: How many ships travel or fish in an area.
criteria.note: Ships are detected one radar image at a time; no open global monthly ship-count series exists.
